subject: Private VPC: residency, retention, and deletion — operational checklist / Q&A
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@harmoniahealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@harmoniahealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment questions: residency & deletion process

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — the VPC walkthrough was helpful. Before we move to procurement we need a concise operations-level summary that we can share with our security and procurement reviewers. Specifically:

1) For a Private (VPC) deployment, where is customer data stored (control plane vs. data plane) and who can access it?
2) What residency guarantees can we sign up for? Can we pin storage to a specific cloud region and ensure no cross-region replication?
3) Retention defaults / tweaks: how do we configure retention windows for request logs, KV caches, and model artifacts?
4) Deletion workflow: please outline the end-to-end deletion path (immediate deletes, soft-delete/retention, secure wipe, attestations).

If you can attach any SOC2 or technical docs that map to these items that would be great.

—Sara
Sara Li
Head of Security Operations
Harmonia Health
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@harmoniahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, procurement@harmoniahealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: residency & deletion process

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short operational checklist and attached supporting docs (SOC2 cert + deletion playbook). High level answers below; happy to hop on a 30-min call with your security team to walk through.

Quick answers (summary):
- Storage separation: control plane metadata (deployment config, billing) is in Redwood control plane (encrypted, access-limited). All customer request/response payloads and KV caches sit in the customer-managed data plane inside your VPC (you control the storage account).
- Residency guarantees: For Private, customers choose a cloud region at provisioning. By default we do not cross-replicate data to other regions for active deployments; cross-region replication only happens when explicitly configured for DR and requires customer approval.
- Retention defaults & tuning: request traces and short-term caches default to 30 days; model artifacts are versioned and retained per your lifecycle policy (default 90 days). We expose retention controls in the deployment manifest and via Console/API; changes are audited.
- Deletion workflow: immediate logical deletion (soft delete) + secure wipe. Steps: 1) API trigger or console request -> soft delete flag, 2) background purge job clears object storage with multi-pass overwrite where supported, 3) KMS-wrapped keys destroyed per customer KMS policy, 4) system generates deletion attestations (timestamped) and logs to audit export.

Attachments included: redwood_private_data_handling_summary.pdf, SOC2-type2-cert-2025.pdf, sample-data-deletion-playbook.md

Next steps I propose:
- 30-min walk-through with your security group (I can bring Lauren from Product and Hannah who owns deployments in us-west)
- Provide a one-page residency commitment we can include in the SOW

Available slots: Thu 4/22 9–11am PT, Thu 4/22 3–4pm PT. Which works?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions

Hi Sara — adding a few operational details you can copy into your control doc.

Operational checklist (for inclusion in SOW / runbook):
- Provisioning: customer picks cloud provider and region (e.g., AWS us-west-2). Deployment manifest records region and subnet IDs; Redwood infra team validates networking during provisioning.
- Network & access: all traffic to the data plane is inside the VPC; we require least-privilege IAM roles for infra engineers. Control plane API calls are limited to metadata only and authenticated via mTLS to customer-managed endpoints.
- Storage controls: object storage buckets (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) are customer-owned; Redwood services are given scoped service principal access for object PUT/GET during runtime. No automatic cross-region replication unless DR enabled by request.
- Encryption & keys: data-at-rest encrypted with customer KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed keys; KMS key rotation and destruction follow cloud vendor semantics and will be documented in the SOW.
- Retention knobs: per-deployment manifest fields: request_log_retention_days, kv_cache_ttl_hours, model_artifact_retention_days. Changes take effect after rolling policy rollout; all changes logged.
- Deletion & attestations: on-demand deletion API -> triggers object deletions + KMS key lifecycle steps -> audit record exported to your SIEM (we can push to S3/CloudWatch/EventHub or a syslog endpoint). We provide a signed attestation PDF within 48 hours of verified purge.

If you want, I can produce the one-page residency commitment language that you can attach to your procurement doc. Confirm the target region and whether DR cross-region replication is acceptable.

—Lauren
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule:

- Can the residency commitment explicitly state: data plane storage will remain in the chosen region (us-west-2) and no automatic replication will occur without documented customer opt-in?
- For deletion attestations: is the 48-hour window guaranteed in the SOW or best-effort? We need guaranteed turnaround for our contract.

If you can provide that one-page commitment (and indicate whether the attestation time can be contractual), we can move to an LOI and route to procurement.

Sara
